mainTopic: Does a קרבן that lost its purpose need explicit עקירה? The גמרא tests this through a ברייתא about a פסח whose owners died, and ends by attributing that ברייתא to יוסף בן חונאי.
overview: The amud asks whether a קרבן that has lost its original purpose needs an explicit עקירה (uprooting) before it becomes a different קרבן. A ברייתא on our משנה rules that a פסח whose owners died, slaughtered on a weekday, is burned immediately. That fits only if עקירה is needed: the animal stays a פסח, so its flaw is in its body (פסולו בגופו). If no עקירה were needed, it would be a שלמים with an outside flaw, and the rule is that such a flaw calls for עיבור צורה (waiting overnight) before burning. So רב's statement about an אשם is corrected to a case slaughtered explicitly לשם עולה. But רבי חייא בר גמדא holds that in general no עקירה is needed, so the ברייתא must be explained for him. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers with נראה ונדחה, which is rejected because רב holds that living animals are not permanently rejected. רב פפא attributes the ברייתא to רבי אליעזר, which is rejected because רבי אליעזר would require a חטאת on שבת. רב אשי links רב to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, but that proof is undercut. The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא follows יוסף בן חונאי, and the chapter אלו דברים ends.

steps.title: A teaching on the משנה: on a weekday the פסח is burned immediately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the משנה about a פסח whose owners died before the blood was thrown. It says that on a weekday such an animal is burned right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא taught about this משנה: on a weekday, in a case like this, it should be burned immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about the פסח whose owners died, and it rules that the animal is burned right away. This is a setup line: the גמרא is about to use this ruling as a test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is 'immediately' (מיד). Some disqualified קרבנות are burned at once, and others must first wait overnight. The גמרא will show that this timing tells us how the animal is legally classified.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא taught about it (about this משנה)
On a weekday (not שבת)
In a case like this
It must be burned immediately

steps.confusionAlert: 'Like this' means the case in the משנה: the פסח was slaughtered, and then it turned out the owners had died. Nobody is left to eat it.

phrases.english: And it was taught regarding it (the mishna):
On a weekday, in a case like this,
phrases.notes: A פסח slaughtered, and then it became known that the owners had died.

phrases.english: it should be burned immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the משנה earlier, to test whether a קרבן with no owners needs עקירה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a קרבן with no owners needs עקירה to change status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the משנה: on a weekday it is burned immediately.

steps.title: The ruling fits well if עקירה is required
steps.stepSummary: If עקירה is needed, the animal is still a פסח. A פסח with no owners has a flaw in its own body (פסולו בגופו), so it is burned right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine if you say עקירה is needed. Then this is still a פסח, and since it has no owners, its flaw is in its body. That is why it is burned immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא makes perfect sense if we hold that עקירה is required. This is the first half of a two-part test ('this works... but that doesn't').
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without explicit עקירה, the animal keeps its status as a פסח. A פסח with no owners is useless in itself, so this counts as פסולו בגופו. Such a flaw calls for immediate burning, which matches the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say...
Uprooting: explicitly removing a קרבן's original identity
Owners of the קרבן
Its flaw is in the קרבן's own body
Because of this, therefore

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it requires uprooting,
this is (still) a Paschal offering,
and since it has no owners —
its disqualification is in its body,
therefore it should be burned immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא fits the view that עקירה is required.
steps.raayaObject: The view that עקירה is required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling of immediate burning fits a פסח that is פסולו בגופו.

steps.title: If no עקירה is needed, the animal should wait overnight first
steps.stepSummary: If no עקירה is needed, the animal became a שלמים automatically. Its only flaw would be that it was slaughtered after the afternoon תמיד, which is an outside problem. That kind of flaw calls for עיבור צורה, not immediate burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say no עקירה is needed, then from the start it was a שלמים. What is its flaw? Something outside the animal: he slaughtered it after the afternoon תמיד. Then it should need עיבור צורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that no עקירה is needed. Under that view, the ברייתא's 'burn immediately' would be wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owners died, the animal would automatically be a שלמים. A שלמים is fine in its body. Its only problem is timing, since nothing may be offered after the afternoon תמיד. Such an outside flaw requires waiting overnight until it becomes נותר, and only then burning.

keyTerms.meaning: From the beginning
Peace-offering; a פסח that lost its status becomes this
Something else: an outside reason, not the animal itself
The daily afternoon offering
Letting its 'form' pass: waiting overnight until it becomes נותר, then burning

steps.confusionAlert: Slaughtering a פסח after the afternoon תמיד is exactly correct. The problem arises only if the animal is now a שלמים, because no שלמים may be offered after that תמיד.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא בָּעֵי עֲקִירָה —
phrases.english: But if you say it does not require uprooting —
from the beginning it was a peace-offering,
its disqualification is because of what?
Because of something else,
that he slaughtered it
after the daily afternoon offering.
It should require that its form decay (wait overnight).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא בָּעֵי עֲקִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the 'בשלמא... אלא' test. It shows that the opposing view does not fit the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (drawn from רב's statement) that a קרבן with no owners needs no עקירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view the animal is a שלמים with only an outside flaw. That requires עיבור צורה, but the ברייתא says to burn it immediately.

steps.title: The general rule: when to burn immediately and when to wait
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states the rule. A flaw in the body means immediate burning. A flaw in the blood or in the owners means waiting overnight (עיבור צורה) first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא taught: this is the rule. Anything whose flaw is in its body is burned immediately. If the flaw is in the blood or the owners, let its form pass, and then it goes out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its attack with a ברייתא that states the burning rule outright. This rule proves the attack from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sorts flaws into two groups. A flaw in the body means burn now. A flaw in the blood or the owners means wait overnight first. A פסח-turned-שלמים, with only a timing flaw, would belong in the 'wait' group. So the ruling 'burn immediately' proves the animal is still a פסח, which means עקירה is required.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
In the blood: a flaw in the blood service
Let its form pass (wait overnight)
The place of burning

steps.whatToRemember: Flaw in the body means burn immediately. Flaw in the blood or the owners means wait overnight, then burn.

phrases.english: As it was taught: this is the principle:
Anything whose disqualification is in its body — it is burned immediately.
In the blood or in the owners —
its form must decay
and then it goes out to the place of burning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim that an outside flaw requires עיבור צורה. This completes the proof against the 'no עקירה' view.
steps.raayaObject: The burning rule used in the קשיא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: 'זה הכלל, כל שפסולו בגופו ישרף מיד...'

steps.title: Re-reading רב's statement: the אשם was slaughtered explicitly as an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its version of רב's statement. רב did not say that slaughtering סתם works. He said that slaughtering explicitly לשם עולה works. This shows that רב requires עקירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, do not say 'he slaughtered it סתם, it is כשר as an עולה.' Say instead 'he slaughtered it לשם עולה, it is כשר.' This shows that עקירה is required.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the 'no עקירה' view was disproven, the גמרא re-reads רב's statement about the אשם. In the new version, the animal was explicitly slaughtered as an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original version suggested that רב holds no עקירה is needed. The ברייתא disproved that. So רב's words are corrected to a case of explicit intent לשם עולה. Now רב agrees that a change of status needs explicit עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say (this version)... rather say (this version)
Without specifying any intent
For the sake of a burnt-offering
Apparently, this shows

steps.whatToRemember: רב's statement is corrected: an אשם counts as an עולה only when it is slaughtered explicitly לשם עולה, so רב requires עקירה. This is not the final word on עקירה. From step 6 on, the גמרא deals with רבי חייא בר גמדא, who holds that in general no עקירה is needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: After this correction, רב holds that a change of קרבן status needs active intent, and a passive change like the owner's atonement is not enough. The next steps show that רבי חייא בר גמדא disagrees in general, so the ברייתא then has to be explained in a different way.

phrases.english: Rather, do not say
'he slaughtered it without specification — it is valid as a burnt-offering,'
but say
'he slaughtered it as a burnt-offering — it is valid.'
Apparently, it requires uprooting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from the ברייתא and corrects the wording of רב's statement to match.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Emendation of the wording of רב's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב held that an אשם slaughtered סתם counts as an עולה, implying no עקירה is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב spoke of an אשם slaughtered explicitly לשם עולה, so he too requires עקירה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the corrected version of his statement, רב requires explicit עקירה for a קרבן with no owners to change status.

steps.title: A challenge from the view of רבי חייא בר גמדא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר גמדא says עקירה is needed only when the owners were pushed off to פסח שני. In every other case, no עקירה is needed. So how do we explain the ברייתא that says the animal is burned right away?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חייא בר גמדא, there is a difficulty. He said that the scholars in the study group concluded as follows. עקירה is needed only in a case where the owners were impure from a dead body and were pushed off to פסח שני. So only that case needs עקירה, and in general no עקירה is needed. What can be said, then, about our ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opinion of רבי חייא בר גמדא and uses it to challenge the ruling that the animal is burned right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר גמדא says only one special case needs עקירה: owners pushed off to פסח שני, who still want to use this animal later. In every other case, a leftover פסח turns into a שלמים by itself. If so, our animal should be a שלמים with only an outside flaw. It should get עיבור צורה, not immediate burning, so the ruling in the ברייתא seems hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusion that came out of a study group's discussion
People who became impure from contact with a dead body
The make-up פסח a month later, for those who could not bring the first one
In general, in ordinary cases
What can be said? A sign that a question is hard to answer

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא בר גמדא is not saying that every פסח needs עקירה. He says the opposite: only the פסח שני case needs it. That is exactly why there is a problem.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda,
who said: it came out from the mouth of the study group, and they said:
for example, where the owners were impure from a dead body
and were pushed off to the second Pesach.
phrases.notes: In this case they surely want to keep the animal for פסח שני.

phrases.english: It is this case that requires uprooting,
but in general it does not require uprooting.
What is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 5 explained the ruling according to רב by having him require עקירה. Now the גמרא turns to a different אמורא who clearly does not require עקירה in general.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a פסח whose owners died is burned right away, according to רבי חייא בר גמדא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no עקירה is needed, the animal is automatically a שלמים with only an outside flaw. An outside flaw calls for עיבור צורה, not immediate burning.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: the animal was rejected after midday
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the animal was set aside before midday and the owners died after midday. So it is נראה ונדחה, and it can never become fit again, even as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where they set aside the animal before midday, and the owners died after midday. That makes it 'fit and then rejected.' Anything that was fit and then rejected never becomes fit again.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers the challenge by placing the ברייתא in a specific case where the animal is permanently rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before midday, an animal set aside for a פסח could still be offered as a שלמים. At midday it became fixed as a פסח, so it was pushed away from being a שלמים. When the owners then died, it was pushed away from being a פסח too. Because of the rule of נראה ונדחה, it can never return, so it is burned right away even without needing עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? The גמרא is about to limit a source to a specific situation
He set it aside (designated the animal)
Midday, when the time for the פסח begins
Fit and then rejected; once rejected, it never becomes fit again

steps.confusionAlert: Midday matters here. Before midday the animal could still be a שלמים. After midday it is locked in as a פסח, so losing the פסח status leaves it with nothing to fall back on.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where they designated it before midday,
and the owners died after midday,
so that it was fit and then rejected.
And anything that was fit and then rejected
never again returns to being fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to designation before midday and death after midday
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal should automatically become a שלמים and only need עיבור צורה
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the animal is permanently rejected through נראה ונדחה, so it is burned right away

steps.title: Challenge: רב holds living animals cannot be permanently rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. This reason is only needed according to רב, and רב himself holds that living animals are not permanently rejected. So נראה ונדחה cannot explain the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this reason needed for anyone except רב? But רב said: living animals are not permanently rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב הונא's answer by pointing to a known ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נראה ונדחה answer is only needed for רב's approach, where the animal would otherwise become a שלמים by itself. But רב holds that the rule of permanent rejection does not apply to a living animal. Our animal is still alive when the problem happens, so it is not permanently rejected, and the answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this reason needed for anyone except...?
Living animals cannot be permanently rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of נראה ונדחה applies to animals that were already slaughtered. According to רב, it does not apply to a living animal. That is why רב הונא's answer about the ruling to burn the animal right away does not work.

phrases.english: Is this reason needed for anyone but Rav?
But Rav said:
living creatures are not permanently rejected.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי הוּא טַעְמָא אֶלָּא לְרַב, הָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the נראה ונדחה explanation for why the animal is burned right away
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב holds that living animals cannot be permanently rejected, so נראה ונדחה does not apply to a live animal

steps.title: רב פפא: the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ברייתא that requires burning right away follows רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר holds that slaughtering other offerings as a פסח makes them invalid, so the flaw is in the animal's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It is רבי אליעזר. He said that one who slaughters other offerings as a פסח makes them invalid. So the flaw is in the body of the animal itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The נראה ונדחה answer just failed. Now רב פפא offers a new answer by naming the תנא behind the ברייתא: רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no עקירה is needed, the animal is already a שלמים, yet the slaughterer killed it with the intent of a פסח. רבי אליעזר holds that slaughtering another offering as a פסח makes it invalid in itself. That is a flaw in its body, so by step 4's rule it is burned right away, even though no עקירה was required.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? (a question that tries to identify the author of a source)
Other offerings slaughtered as a פסח
Its flaw is in its body (the offering itself is defective)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Whose opinion is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: וְכֵן הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֲחֵרִים לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח — פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: who said: And likewise, one who slaughters other offerings as a Pesach makes them invalid,
so its flaw is in its body.
phrases.notes: This connects back to the rule in step 4 that a flaw in the body means immediate burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected נראה ונדחה answer from step 8 with a new answer about who authored the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to contradict רבי חייא בר גמדא's view that no עקירה is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, for whom the flaw is in the animal's body.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר would also require a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, the slaughterer should also have to bring a חטאת. רבי אליעזר does not accept the rule that one who errs while doing a מצוה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is רבי אליעזר, the person should also be liable to bring a חטאת. After all, רבי אליעזר does not hold that one who makes a mistake while doing a מצוה is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's answer. If the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, it should also say the slaughterer brings a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering an invalid offering on שבת is a desecration of שבת. Some say a person who erred while trying to do a מצוה is exempt. רבי אליעזר disagrees with that rule. Our משנה rules that on שבת the slaughterer is exempt, so the משנה with its ברייתא cannot follow רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering, brought for an accidental sin
Is liable
One who errs while doing a מצוה is exempt

phrases.english: But if it is Rabbi Eliezer,
he would also be liable to bring a sin-offering,
for Rabbi Eliezer does not hold
that one who errs regarding a מצוה is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא, חַטָּאת נָמֵי מִחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's choice of רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the ברייתא to רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's other view (no exemption for one who errs in a מצוה) clashes with the משנה, which exempts the slaughterer on שבת from a חטאת.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows יוסף בן חונאי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרב סלא חסידא says the ברייתא follows יוסף בן חונאי. Like רבי אליעזר, he holds that offerings slaughtered as a פסח or as a חטאת are invalid, so the flaw is in the body. But on exemptions from a חטאת he holds like רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף בריה דרב סלא חסידא explained it before רב פפא: This ברייתא is יוסף בן חונאי. As we learned, יוסף בן חונאי says that offerings slaughtered as a פסח or as a חטאת are invalid. So the flaw is in the body, and that is why it is burned right away. On exemptions, he holds like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer fixes the problem. It names a תנא who agrees with רבי אליעזר about the flaw but disagrees with him about the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף בן חונאי gives us exactly the mix the ברייתא needs. Because the flaw is in the animal's body, it is burned right away. Because he holds like רבי יהושע that one who errs in a מצוה is exempt, no חטאת is required.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it
A תנא who agrees with רבי אליעזר about this flaw
Evidently / this shows
Exemptions (here, from bringing a חטאת)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that requires immediate burning follows יוסף בן חונאי. For him the flaw is in the body, and on exemptions he holds like רבי יהושע, so no חטאת is needed.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, תַּרְגְּמָא רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef son of Rav Salla the Ḥasid explained it
before Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַנִּי יוֹסֵף בֶּן חוֹנַאי הִיא.
phrases.english: Whose opinion is this? It is Yosef ben Ḥonai.
As we learned in a mishna, Yosef ben Ḥonai says:

phrases.aramaic: הַנִּשְׁחָטִים לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח וּלְשֵׁם חַטָּאת — פְּסוּלִים,
phrases.english: Offerings slaughtered as a Pesach or as a sin-offering are invalid.
Evidently, its flaw is in its body,
and that is why it is burned right away.
But on exemptions, he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע holds that one who errs while doing a מצוה is exempt from a חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, תַּרְגְּמָא רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 10 by naming a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attributing the ברייתא to a תנא with a split position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only רבי אליעזר holds that this flaw is in the body, and he would require a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: יוסף בן חונאי agrees about the flaw but follows רבי יהושע on the exemption.

steps.title: רב אשי: רב follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי takes a different approach. He says רב's ruling follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. That תנא says that if there was still time in the day to find out whether the owners withdrew, died, or became impure, the slaughterer is liable. The animal must also wait overnight before burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רב spoke according to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. As a ברייתא teaches, he says: If there was still time in the day to find out whether the owners withdrew, died, or became impure, the slaughterer is liable. Its form must be left to decay overnight, and then it is taken out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a separate answer. He ties רב to a תנא who requires waiting overnight in these cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי ישמעאל's case, the owners withdrew, died, or became impure. He says the person who slaughtered on שבת is liable, since he could have checked first. The animal is not burned right away; it waits overnight (עיבור צורה), which matches step 4's rule for a flaw in the owners.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough time
They withdrew (the owners removed themselves from the offering)
Its form must decay (wait overnight before burning)
The place of burning

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה.
phrases.english: Rav spoke according to Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As a baraita teaches, Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:
If there is still time in the day

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם מָשְׁכוּ בְּעָלִים אֶת יְדֵיהֶם
phrases.english: to find out whether the owners withdrew
or died or became impure, he is liable,
and its form must decay, and then it goes out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the original challenge against רב (steps 3 to 4). Instead of changing the wording of רב's statement (step 5), it says רב follows a תנא who does not require עקירה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking רב's ruling to a tannaitic source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's ruling to burn the animal immediately seemed to refute רב's view that no עקירה is needed, which forced the change in the wording of his statement (step 5).
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, a תנא who requires עיבור צורה in these cases and so seems to hold that no עקירה is needed, against our ברייתא.

steps.title: The reason: no uprooting is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל requires waiting overnight. It answers that this must be because he holds no עקירה is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Is it not because no עקירה is needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב אשי's point. It shows the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's ruling: he does not require עקירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no עקירה is needed, the animal could automatically count as a שלמים. So the flaw is not in its body, and it is not burned right away. Instead it waits overnight until it becomes leftover meat (נותר), and only then is it burned.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Is it not because…? (introduces the obvious reason)
Uprooting, meaning explicitly removing the animal's status as a פסח

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's proof: רבי ישמעאל requires waiting overnight, which seems to show he holds no עקירה is needed, and רב follows him. Steps 14–15 reject this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: Waiting overnight does not mean the animal is acceptable. It still gets burned. The wait only shows that the flaw is not in the animal's body.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because it does not need uprooting!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא בָּעֵי עֲקִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reasoning out of the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל holds no עקירה is needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling that the animal must wait overnight (תעובר צורתו) instead of being burned right away

steps.title: Waiting overnight may have a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 13. רבי ישמעאל may require waiting overnight because he agrees with the תנא דבי רבה בר אבוה, who says even פיגול must wait overnight. That rule is learned from the matching word עון, which appears both by פיגול and by נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that? Maybe he holds like the תנא from the school of רבה בר אבוה, who said that even פיגול also needs to wait overnight. He learns this from the word 'עון' (sin) used by פיגול and the same word used by נותר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from Step 13. Waiting overnight does not have to mean that רבי ישמעאל holds no עקירה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that if the animal must wait overnight, the flaw is not in its body, so no עקירה is needed. But there is an opinion that even פיגול, whose flaw is clearly in the body, must wait overnight before burning. If רבי ישמעאל holds that view, waiting overnight proves nothing about עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (opens a rejection)
Perhaps
An offering made invalid by wrong intent about when it will be eaten
Letting the meat sit overnight until its appearance changes, and only then burning it
Sacrificial meat left over past its allowed time
'Sin', the shared word used for the גזירה שוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two waiting rules. Usually a flaw in the body means burn right away. The תנא דבי רבה בר אבוה is an exception: he requires waiting overnight even for פיגול, because of a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
Perhaps it is because he holds
like the Tanna of the school of Rabba bar Avuh,
who said: even piggul
also requires waiting overnight for its form to change.
For he derives 'iniquity'–'iniquity' from leftover meat.
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the word עון shows up by פיגול (ויקרא ז:יח) and by נותר (ויקרא יט:ז).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference that waiting overnight means no עקירה is needed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Waiting overnight can also be explained by the גזירה שוה of עון–עון, which requires it even when the flaw is in the body

steps.title: Impure owners show that this reading must be right
steps.stepSummary: In the case where the owners became impure, everyone agrees that עקירה is needed. רבי חייא בר גמדא taught this about owners impure from a dead body, who are pushed off to פסח שני. Yet רבי ישמעאל still requires waiting overnight. So he must hold like the תנא דבי רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you don't say this, what can you say about the case where the owners became impure? There it certainly needs עקירה. For רבי חייא בר גמדא said that this came out of the group of scholars: for example, when the owners were impure from a dead body and were pushed off to פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection with proof. Even in a case where עקירה is clearly needed, רבי ישמעאל still requires waiting overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owners are impure from a dead body, their animal is still set aside as a פסח for פסח שני. So using it as a different offering would require עקירה. רבי ישמעאל still requires waiting overnight in this case, so his overnight rule cannot depend on whether עקירה is needed. It must come from the עון–עון rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you don't say so (introduces proof that you must say so)
The owners became ritually impure
Actively removing the animal's status as a פסח
It came out of (was stated by) the group of scholars
The make-up פסח a month later, for those who could not bring the first one

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
in the case where the owners became impure, what is there to say?
That case certainly requires uprooting,
for Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said:
it was thrown out from the group of scholars,
such as where the owners were impure from a corpse
and were pushed off to the second Pesach.

steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל's overnight requirement comes from the תנא דבי רבה בר אבוה, not from a view that no עקירה is needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר גמדא: owners impure from a corpse, pushed to פסח שני, need עקירה
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the basis for רב אשי's approach. רבי ישמעאל's opinion no longer tells us anything about עקירה.

steps.title: Back to the original answer: יוסף בן חונאי
steps.stepSummary: Since רב אשי's approach does not hold up, the גמרא concludes as answered earlier: the ברייתא follows יוסף בן חונאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at first: it follows יוסף בן חונאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב אשי's approach. It returns to the answer of רב יוסף בריה דרב סלא חסידא from Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף בן חונאי holds that the flaw is in the body, so the animal is burned right away. He also holds like רבי יהושע, so the slaughterer who erred while doing a מצוה is exempt from a חטאת. This answer explains both parts of the ברייתא without problems.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is clear (the final conclusion)
As was answered at the beginning
The תנא whose view explains the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: the ברייתא that requires burning right away, with no חטאת, follows יוסף בן חונאי. The flaw is in the body, as רבי אליעזר holds, and the slaughterer is exempt, as רבי יהושע holds.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as he answered at the beginning:
it is the view of Yosef ben Chonai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since Steps 14–15 undercut רב אשי's approach, the גמרא returns to Step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows יוסף בן חונאי

steps.title: הדרן: closing the chapter אלו דברים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter אלו דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter אלו דברים.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן עלך is a traditional farewell said at the end of each chapter. It expresses the hope to return and learn the chapter again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (chapter-closing formula)
Name of the chapter (the sixth chapter of פסחים)

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'These Matters'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final conclusion
